attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “This is [5, Theorem 3.8], with the same uniform product measure, Fourier degree, simplex, and Gaussian normalization.” Its bibliography: “[5] S. Khot and A. Naor, Approximate kernel clustering, Mathematika 55 (2009), no. 1–2, 129–165. doi:10.1112/S002557930000098X.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 6.2 (Khot–Naor low-influence bound) of the manuscript “The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension” (preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 096 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b546ae5fd2ea7011), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For fixed k and every η > 0, there exists 0 < τ0 < 1/2, independent of r, such that every r ∈ N and every f : Ωr → ∆k satisfying Inf ≤log(1/τ0) j (fi) ≤ τ0 (i ∈ [k], j ∈ [r]) obey OBJ(f) ≤ Ck + η.
